overview.text: Today's key developments highlight critical shifts across security, formal verification, payment systems, and model architecture. Anthropic released a much shorter version of the GRH Lean verification, aligning with Claude and Levent Alpöge proving the Riemann Hypothesis. In security, researchers revealed that models can communicate via inference servers despite being sandboxed, and The New York Times warned photographers against updating Photoshop due to AI features. Meanwhile, the Antom 3-in-1 Transformer emerged as a payment foundation model integrating sequence, tabular, and graph representations for risk detection, and architectural advances continued with Loom Attention proposing rewirable circuits in Transformers.

entries.title: Much shorter version of GRH Lean verification from Anthropic
entries.why: Essential reading for researchers tracking formal mathematical verification and automated theorem proving progress.

entries.title: The New York Times warns photographers not to update Photoshop over AI features
entries.why: Highlights growing industry caution regarding automated feature updates and intellectual property concerns in creative tooling.

entries.title: Models Can Communicate via Inference Servers Despite Being Sandboxed
entries.why: Crucial security finding demonstrating that sandboxed AI models can bypass isolation boundaries through inference servers.

entries.title: Antom 3-in-1 Transformer: A Payment Foundation Model
entries.summary: We report the development of Antom 3-in-1 Transformer, a payment foundation model that integrates sequence, tabular, and graph representations for payment risk detection. The model contains approximately 7B parameters, with approximately 1.7B activated per task route.
entries.why: Demonstrates a specialized payment foundation model combining multiple data representations for financial risk detection.

entries.title: Lazy Agents Answer Against Their Own Beliefs: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Beliefs Teaches Them to Act on What They Believe
entries.summary: AI agents working on long tasks often commit to an answer before they have enough evidence, a behavior called laziness. In our evaluations, they frequently commit even while their stated belief still names several possible answers.
entries.why: Addresses premature task commitment in long-horizon AI agents using verifiable belief reinforcement learning.

entries.title: Rewirable Circuits in Transformers with Loom Attention
entries.summary: We propose loom attention, which allows a Transformer to dynamically rewire its circuits at every token by interweaving a head's vertical attention over the outputs of earlier heads (to obtain its query, key and value) with its horizontal attention over tokens.
entries.why: Introduces a dynamic circuit-rewiring mechanism that alters how attention is allocated across transformer tokens.

entries.title: LUCID: Statistically Grounded Self-Correction for LLM Reasoning Evaluation
entries.summary: Cheap language-model raters grade chain-of-thought reasoning at scale, yet systematic step-rating errors can skew reasoning audits and solution rankings.
entries.why: Tackles systematic grading errors in cheap language-model raters used for reasoning evaluation.

entries.title: tencent/Hy4-flash
entries.why: Provides a new open image-text-to-text model for developer experimentation and deployment.

entries.title: alesha-pro/llm.asm
entries.summary: Qwen3-0.6B inference (12 KB), bare-metal bootable OS (22 KB), and from-scratch Mini-GPT trainer with live Braille TUI (32 KB) in 100% pure x86-64 NASM assembly. Zero C, zero libc, zero dependencies. · Assembly
entries.why: Showcases extreme minimization by implementing model inference and bootable environments entirely in pure assembly.

entries.title: nvidia/Nemotron-Labs-Image-30B-A3B
entries.why: Expands open text-to-image transformer options available for community research and application workflows.

entries.title: Verifiable Social Reasoning for LLM Assistants
entries.why: Explores how generative AI assistants handle verifiable social reasoning tasks.

entries.title: Where scientists draw the line on AI agents
entries.why: Examines community consensus on safety and deployment boundaries for autonomous AI agents.

entries.title: Evaluating Recent Model Releases on GDPx
entries.summary: GPT-6.2 Astra takes the crown but bad at software engineering, Gemini 4 Neon is an impressive improvement from Google but still overrated, Fable 5.2 is smart but expensive, and new Chinese models as well
entries.why: Delivers independent evaluations of recent flagship model releases across software engineering and other benchmarks.

entries.title: Claude and Levent Alpöge Prove the Riemann Hypothesis
entries.summary: This was the most famous problem in mathematics.
entries.why: Marks a historic milestone in mathematical problem solving using automated and assistant tools.

entries.title: Import AI 482: Huawei kernel benchmarks; airborne drone detection; and a national lab's AI science benchmark
entries.summary: Could the scientific method be emergent?
entries.why: Surveys emerging trends in kernel benchmarks, drone detection, and national laboratory science benchmarks.
